title: Photosynthesis
description: How plants turn light, water, and CO2 into sugar and oxygen.

# Photosynthesis

Photosynthesis is the process by which plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.

## Summary equation

6 CO2 + 6 H2O + light -> C6H12O6 + 6 O2

That is: six molecules of carbon dioxide and six molecules of water, powered by light energy, produce one molecule of glucose and six molecules of oxygen.

## Two main stages

1. **Light reactions** — occur in the thylakoid membranes of the chloroplast. Chlorophyll absorbs light; water is split (photolysis), releasing O2; energy is stored as ATP and NADPH. The oxygen we breathe comes from splitting WATER, not from CO2.
2. **Dark reactions (Calvin cycle)** — occur in the stroma of the chloroplast and do NOT require light directly; they use the ATP and NADPH from the light reactions to fix CO2 into glucose.

## The role of chlorophyll

Chlorophyll is the green pigment that absorbs red and blue light and reflects green — which is why leaves look green. Chlorophyll only captures light energy; it is not a raw material that becomes sugar.

## Factors affecting the rate

Light intensity, CO2 concentration, and temperature. Beyond a certain point the rate saturates even if more light is added.
